newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu indictment may force election - minister.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu indictment may force election - minister.

text.p: An Israeli cabinet minister close to Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday the country may be forced to hold elections if prosecutors accept police recommendations to charge the prime minister with fraud.
Asked what would happen if prosecutors pressed charges, Health Minister Yehoshua Matza told Israel Radio in English: "Perhaps it will be to go back to elections."
Matza said there would be no other option since under a law first applied in balloting last May, the prime minister is chosen directly in a poll separate from parliamentary elections.
Matza said that even with the police recommendation, made public on Wednesday night, the government can stay in office.
"Of course it can go on because it's only a recommendation. The final decision will be taken by the attorney general and we have to wait for his decision."

Asked if the prime minister should not resign because of the seriousness of the affair, Matza said: "No. We are a state of law. And we have to wait as I have said for the resolution, for the decision of the attorney general."
